context.story_title: User Can View and Restore Soft-Deleted Courses
context.section_tech_spec_epic_2_relevance: This story directly addresses Acceptance Criteria 8 from `tech-spec-epic-2.md`: "The system provides a mechanism to restore a soft-deleted course (e.g., from a 'Trash' view)." The implementation should leverage the `restoreCourse` method defined in the `ICourseManager` interface. The `courses` table uses the `deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column to track soft-deleted status.
context.section_architecture_relevance: As per `solution-architecture.md`, the Next.js frontend will communicate directly with Supabase via `supabase-js`. All database operations for courses are protected by Row Level Security (RLS) policies to ensure users can only modify their own courses. The `restoreCourse` operation will be an `UPDATE` query that sets the `deleted_at` timestamp back to `NULL`.

code_snippets.sql_table_definition: CREATE TABLE public.courses ( id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, name TEXT NOT NULL, syllabus TEXT, exam_date DATE, deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ, -- Crucial for soft delete/restore created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() );

sql_rls_policy.name: Enable all access for own courses

code_snippets.sql_rls_policy: CREATE POLICY "Enable all access for own courses" ON public.courses FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
code_snippets.javascript_supabase_filter_example_delet: // Example of fetching soft-deleted courses for the "Trash" view const { data: deletedCourses, error } = await supabase .from('courses') .select('*') .not('deleted_at', 'is', null); // Filter for deleted courses

context.ui_ux_considerations: The UI for this story should: - Provide a clear entry point to the "Trash" or "Archived" view from the main Course Management page. - The "Trash" view should clearly list soft-deleted courses, perhaps with an indication of when they were deleted. - Each entry in the "Trash" view should have an easily discoverable "Restore" button or action. - Upon successful restoration, the course should visually move from the "Trash" view back to the active course list. - A non-intrusive success notification (toast) after restoration is recommended. - Since restoration is a non-destructive action, a high-friction confirmation is not required.
context.developer_notes: - Ensure the `restoreCourse` method performs an `UPDATE` operation on the `public.courses` table, setting the `deleted_at` column to `NULL`. - Implement the "Trash" view by querying `courses` where `deleted_at IS NOT NULL`. - Verify that the main active course list correctly displays restored courses and continues to hide soft-deleted ones. - Thoroughly test RLS: ensure a user cannot restore a course belonging to another user. - Consider error handling and displaying user-friendly messages for failed restore operations.
